phases.title: Module 1: Cluster Foundations
phases.description: Learn the objects and discovery commands that every Kubernetes operator uses.

quests.title: Discover your cluster
quests.description: Start with the broadest read-only check: list the nodes that make up the training cluster.
quests.objective: List Kubernetes nodes and identify their readiness state.
hints: Use kubectl get followed by the plural resource name.
Nodes are cluster-scoped resources; no namespace flag is needed.
Run: kubectl get nodes
quests.simulatedOutput:
NAME      STATUS   ROLES           AGE   VERSION
node-01   Ready    control-plane   42d   v1.29.4

quests.title: Explore namespaces
quests.description: List namespaces to see how Kubernetes separates system and application resources.
quests.objective: Display every namespace in the cluster.
hints: Namespaces are abbreviated as ns.
kubectl accepts both namespace and ns.
Run: kubectl get namespaces
quests.simulatedOutput:
NAME              STATUS   AGE
default           Active   42d
kube-system       Active   42d
k8s-lab           Active   3d

quests.title: Inspect the API surface
quests.description: Use API discovery to see the resource types your kubectl client can work with.
quests.objective: List supported resource types from the API server.
hints: kubectl includes a command specifically for API discovery.
This command does not need get.
Run: kubectl api-resources
quests.simulatedOutput:
NAME                  SHORTNAMES   APIVERSION   NAMESPACED   KIND
pods                  po           v1           true         Pod
deployments           deploy       apps/v1      true         Deployment
services              svc          v1           true         Service
persistentvolumeclaims pvc         v1           true         PersistentVolumeClaim

quests.title: Read a Pod manifest
quests.description: Inspect a running Pod in YAML form so you can distinguish desired specification from observed status.
quests.objective: Request the web Pod as YAML.
hints: The -o flag changes kubectl output format.
YAML is requested with -o yaml.
Run: kubectl get pod web -o yaml
quests.simulatedOutput:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: web
  namespace: default
spec:
  containers:
  - image: nginx:1.25
    name: web
status:
  phase: Running

phases.title: Module 2: Pods & Workloads
phases.description: Create Pods, then use controllers to keep application workloads available and scalable.

quests.title: Create an nginx Pod
quests.description: Create a single Pod named web using the nginx image. This is useful for experimentation, but not for high availability.
quests.objective: Create the web Pod with kubectl run.
hints: kubectl run creates a Pod when no restart policy is supplied.
The Pod name comes immediately after run.
Run: kubectl run web --image=nginx
quests.simulatedOutput: pod/web created

quests.title: Inspect Pod health
quests.description: Read the current Pods and their phase before making a workload change.
quests.objective: List Pods in the current namespace.
hints: Pods have the short name po.
Use the plural resource name after get.
Run: kubectl get pods
quests.simulatedOutput:
NAME   READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
web    1/1     Running   0          20s

quests.title: Deploy a web application
quests.description: Apply the provided Deployment manifest. A Deployment owns ReplicaSets and enables controlled rollout behavior.
quests.objective: Create the web Deployment from a manifest.
hints: Declarative resources are usually created with kubectl apply.
The supplied manifest filename is deployment.yaml.
Run: kubectl apply -f deployment.yaml
quests.simulatedOutput: deployment.apps/web configured

quests.title: Scale a Deployment
quests.description: Increase the web Deployment to three replicas and let the controller reconcile the desired count.
hints: kubectl scale accepts a resource type and resource name.
The desired number uses the --replicas flag.
Run: kubectl scale deployment web --replicas=3
quests.simulatedOutput:
deployment.apps/web scaled

NAME   READY   UP-TO-DATE   AVAILABLE   AGE
web    3/3     3            3           2m

phases.title: Module 3: Configuration & Security
phases.description: Separate configuration and credentials from container images, then examine access control.

quests.title: Inspect ConfigMaps
quests.description: List ConfigMaps to identify non-sensitive configuration available to workloads.
hints: ConfigMap has the short name cm.
Use the plural resource name after get.
Run: kubectl get configmaps
quests.simulatedOutput:
NAME             DATA   AGE
app-settings     3      1d
kube-root-ca.crt 1      42d

quests.title: Create application configuration
quests.description: Create a ConfigMap called app-settings from literal key/value pairs.
hints: kubectl create configmap supports literal data.
The key/value is supplied with --from-literal=KEY=VALUE.
Run: kubectl create configmap app-settings --from-literal=LOG_LEVEL=info
quests.simulatedOutput: configmap/app-settings created

quests.title: Inspect a Secret safely
quests.description: Describe the database Secret without printing its decoded values.
hints: Describe shows metadata and key names, not secret values.
The resource is singular: secret.
Run: kubectl describe secret db-credentials
quests.simulatedOutput:
Name:         db-credentials
Namespace:    default
Type:         Opaque
Data
====
password:  16 bytes
username:  5 bytes

quests.title: Check your authorization
quests.description: Ask the API server whether the current identity may list Pods.
quests.objective: Test RBAC permission to list Pods.
hints: kubectl auth can-i tests an RBAC action without changing state.
Use a verb first, then the resource.
Run: kubectl auth can-i list pods
quests.simulatedOutput: yes

phases.title: Module 4: Storage & Persistence
phases.description: Provision durable storage with StorageClasses and PVCs, then diagnose a common provisioning failure.

quests.title: Inspect StorageClasses
quests.description: Find the default dynamic provisioner and understand how it binds volumes.
hints: StorageClass is abbreviated sc.
The default class is marked in the NAME column.
Run: kubectl get storageclasses
quests.simulatedOutput:
NAME                 PROVISIONER             RECLAIMPOLICY   VOLUMEBINDINGMODE
standard (default)   rancher.io/local-path   Delete          WaitForFirstConsumer

quests.title: Describe the default class
quests.description: Inspect the standard StorageClass to confirm the provisioner and volume-binding behavior.
hints: Use describe for detailed resource metadata.
StorageClass is cluster-scoped, so omit -n.
Run: kubectl describe storageclass standard
quests.simulatedOutput:
Name:            standard
IsDefaultClass:  Yes
Provisioner:     rancher.io/local-path
ReclaimPolicy:   Delete
VolumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer

quests.title: Provision a PVC
quests.description: Apply the PVC manifest and request 1Gi of persistent storage for the application.
hints: PVC manifests declare storage requirements, not a backing disk name.
Use apply so the command can safely be repeated.
Run: kubectl apply -f pvc.yaml
quests.simulatedOutput:
persistentvolumeclaim/app-data created

NAME       STATUS   VOLUME                                     CAPACITY   ACCESS MODES   STORAGECLASS
app-data   Bound    pvc-7c1a2d4e-9f40-4a1c-bc19-1a3f8f0c9c11   1Gi        RWO            standard

quests.title: Diagnose a Pending claim
quests.description: Inspect stuck-data to find why provisioning failed before applying the corrected claim manifest.
hints: PVC is the short name for PersistentVolumeClaim.
The Events section usually gives the root cause.
Run: kubectl describe pvc stuck-data
quests.simulatedOutput:
Name:          stuck-data
Status:        Pending
StorageClass:  fast-ssd
Events:
  Warning  ProvisioningFailed  persistentvolume-controller  storageclass.storage.k8s.io "fast-ssd" not found

phases.title: Module 5: Networking & Services
phases.description: Expose Pods internally and externally, then inspect the endpoints selected by a Service.

quests.title: Inspect Pod IPs
quests.description: List Pods with node and IP information before creating a Service selector.
hints: The normal Pod list hides networking information.
Use the -o wide output option.
Run: kubectl get pods -o wide
quests.simulatedOutput:
NAME       READY   STATUS    IP            NODE
web-abc    1/1     Running   10.244.0.12   node-01
web-def    1/1     Running   10.244.0.13   node-01

quests.title: Create a ClusterIP Service
quests.description: Expose the web Deployment inside the cluster on port 80 using its app=web label.
hints: A Service selects Pods through labels.
The provided manifest is named service.yaml.
Run: kubectl apply -f service.yaml
quests.simulatedOutput: service/web created

quests.title: Verify Service endpoints
quests.description: Confirm the web Service selected healthy backend Pod IPs.
quests.objective: Inspect EndpointSlices for the web Service.
hints: Modern Kubernetes represents backends as EndpointSlice resources.
This command shows the IPs selected by Services.
Run: kubectl get endpointslices
quests.simulatedOutput:
NAME             ADDRESSTYPE   PORTS   ENDPOINTS                 AGE
web-7qpk8        IPv4          80      10.244.0.12,10.244.0.13  10s

quests.title: Inspect an Ingress
quests.description: Describe the web Ingress to understand host and path routing at the edge.
hints: Ingress is an HTTP routing resource, not a Service type.
Describe includes the host, paths, and backend Service.
Run: kubectl describe ingress web
quests.simulatedOutput:
Name:             web
Ingress Class:    nginx
Rules:
  Host              Path  Backends
  app.example.test  /     web:80 (10.244.0.12:80,10.244.0.13:80)

phases.title: Module 6: Operations & Troubleshooting
phases.description: Use events, logs, rollout status, and resource usage to operate workloads with confidence.

quests.title: Review recent events
quests.description: Sort events by timestamp to see the latest scheduling and controller activity first.
quests.objective: Display namespace events in time order.
hints: Events explain what Kubernetes did and why.
The --sort-by field can order output by metadata.creationTimestamp.
Run: kubectl get events --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp
quests.simulatedOutput:
LAST SEEN   TYPE     REASON    OBJECT             MESSAGE
14s         Normal   Scheduled pod/web-abc        Successfully assigned default/web-abc to node-01
11s         Normal   Pulled    pod/web-abc        Container image "nginx:1.25" already present

quests.title: Read application logs
quests.description: Retrieve the current logs from the web Pod to inspect application behavior.
hints: Logs are collected from a container in a Pod.
For a single-container Pod, the container name is optional.
Run: kubectl logs web-abc
quests.simulatedOutput:
/docker-entrypoint.sh: Configuration complete; ready for start up
2026/08/30 11:30:04 [notice] 1#1: nginx/1.25.4
2026/08/30 11:30:04 [notice] 1#1: start worker processes

quests.title: Watch a rollout
quests.description: Wait for the web Deployment rollout to report that all desired replicas are available.
hints: kubectl rollout has commands for status, history, undo, and restart.
Provide the resource and name after status.
Run: kubectl rollout status deployment web
quests.simulatedOutput: deployment "web" successfully rolled out

quests.title: Inspect resource consumption
quests.description: Read live CPU and memory usage reported for Pods by metrics-server.
quests.objective: Show current Pod CPU and memory usage.
hints: kubectl top queries the metrics API rather than Pod status.
Use the plural resource after top.
Run: kubectl top pods
quests.simulatedOutput:
NAME      CPU(cores)   MEMORY(bytes)
web-abc   3m           18Mi
web-def   2m           17Mi
